Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data Scientist with experience in forecasting, churn modelling and experimentation. Uses Python, BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench to develop analytical models and scheduled workflows, with measurable results in forecast accuracy and customer retention. Brings practical feature-engineering experience, automated testing with pytest, and experience building a Dockerised Streamlit experiment tool in collaboration with a data platform team. Holds an MSc in Statistics.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and analysis: Python, SQL, R
Machine learning: LightGBM, XGBoost, feature engineering, SHAP, scikit-learn, pandas
Cloud and data: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt
Software and tools: pytest, Docker, Streamlit, statsmodels, R Markdown, Looker
Additional learning: PyTorch, torchvision

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox | 2022–Present
- Developed a weekly recipe-demand forecasting workflow predicting orders by recipe and region six weeks ahead, using LightGBM with calendar, price and menu-position features.
- Scheduled the forecasting notebook in Vertex AI Workbench to write forecasts to BigQuery for operations reporting in Looker.
- Improved forecast WAPE from 23% to 14%; the work was associated with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste.
- Built a churn propensity model using XGBoost; weekly scores are generated in BigQuery, with retention offers targeted to customers in the top decile.
- Evaluated retention targeting using a 10% holdout; churn was 2.1 percentage points lower in the treated group.
- Developed a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests, used by approximately 25 people in product and growth. Wrote the app and its Dockerfile; the data platform team handles deployment on Cloud Run.
- Began writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code in 2025; coverage is approximately 60%.
- Delivered the internal training session “Stats for PMs” three times.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail | 2020–2022
- Segmented customers and analysed tariffs using R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days each month.

SELECTED PROJECT
Image Classification Course Project | Personal | 2025
- Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food-images dataset as part of an online deep-learning course; achieved approximately 80% accuracy.
- Tools: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab.

EDUCATION
MSc in Statistics
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional and unusually strong in using quantified outcomes: WAPE improved from 23% to 14%, estimated food waste reduced by 9%, churn reduced by 2.1 percentage points, and the Streamlit tool was used by approximately 25 people. The experience bullets clearly distinguish the candidate's direct responsibilities from the data platform team's deployment responsibility, which supports credibility. The document also accurately presents the candidate as a Data Scientist transitioning toward Machine Learning Engineering rather than overstating production engineering experience. Minor completeness limitations include placeholder contact details and limited context about the employer or education institution, but no unsupported skills or experiences were detected when cross-referenced with the supplied candidate information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, reverse-chronological experience, simple bullets and searchable technology names. It includes strong keywords such as Python, SQL, LightGBM, XGBoost, feature engineering, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Docker, Streamlit, pytest, dbt and Cloud Run. AI screening probability is moderate rather than high for this specific role: the document will likely be recognised as a Data Scientist profile with relevant cloud, modelling and experimentation experience, but screening may reject it because terms such as chat assistants, RAG, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLflow, Kubeflow and Airflow are absent. These are genuine experience gaps, not keywords that should be added without evidence. The ATS position could be improved by making the existing scheduling, batch scoring, orchestration and deployment terms more explicit.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with Python-based machine learning, feature engineering, GCP data tools, experimentation, model evaluation, automated testing, batch scoring and collaboration with a data platform team. It also demonstrates ownership, pragmatic delivery and internal knowledge sharing, which are consistent with the company's emphasis on ownership, teamwork and learning. However, the fit for this particular Machine Learning Engineer role is limited by several substantive gaps: the candidate has not shown four years as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping ML systems through production, has no chat-assistant or RAG experience, has not personally deployed a model as an API, and has no demonstrated model monitoring or data-versioning experience. The supplied material also does not establish a machine learning, computer science or engineering degree; it establishes an MSc in Statistics. GCP exposure is shown through BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, but the candidate's notes correctly limit this claim to practical use rather than broad GCP infrastructure expertise. The role is therefore a credible adjacent or junior/transition-level application, but not a close match to the stated must-have requirements.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified; the CV contains no apparent hallucinated skills, tools or experience.

MINOR BUT MEANINGFUL IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the contact header, replace “[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]” with the candidate’s actual professional contact details before submission. Keep the same simple pipe-separated format so the information remains ATS-readable.
2. In the Professional Summary, make the existing production-relevant scope more explicit without claiming API deployment. For example, change “Uses Python, BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench to develop analytical models and scheduled workflows” to “Uses Python, BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench to develop analytical models, scheduled notebook jobs and batch-scoring workflows.” This better reflects the documented forecasting and churn implementations.
3. In the Technical Skills section under “Cloud and data,” change “BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt” to “BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench scheduled notebooks, dbt Cloud scheduler, dbt, Cloud Run.” All of these are supported by the candidate’s portfolio or notes, and this wording improves matching for cloud and orchestration-related screening without implying broad GCP infrastructure expertise.
4. In the Thistlebox experience section, make the batch-processing architecture more searchable. In the churn bullet, change “weekly scores are generated in BigQuery” to “generated weekly through batch scoring in BigQuery, with retention offers targeted to customers in the top decile.” In the forecasting bullet, retain the existing Vertex AI Workbench and BigQuery wording, but use “scheduled notebook job” rather than only “scheduled the forecasting notebook.”
5. In the Streamlit bullet, retain the explicit boundary around deployment and make the serving-related terminology clearer. Change it to: “Developed and Dockerised a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests; wrote the application and Dockerfile, while the data platform team deployed and operated it on Cloud Run; used by approximately 25 people in product and growth.” This remains truthful and makes the candidate’s direct ownership versus platform ownership unmistakable.
6. In the Professional Summary or Technical Skills section, describe the testing experience with its actual scope rather than the broad phrase “automated testing.” For example, change the summary wording to “introduced pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage.” This is more precise and avoids any implication of mature CI/CD ownership.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured and professionally written CV. The summary is targeted to data science and machine learning, the skills are grouped logically, and the experience bullets use strong evidence such as WAPE improving from 23% to 14%, an estimated 9% food-waste reduction, and a 2.1-percentage-point reduction in churn. The document is also appropriately transparent about the candidate’s current level of production ownership: it states that the data platform team handles Cloud Run deployment and that pytest coverage is approximately 60%. The main limitation is not writing quality but the substantial difference between the candidate’s current Data Scientist experience and the role’s requirements for production ML engineering, AI assistants/RAG and production model operations.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly headings, standard text formatting, conventional chronology and searchable technical keywords. It should parse reliably. AI-screening probability is moderate rather than high: the document contains Python, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Docker, feature engineering, testing and scheduled workflows, but it does not explicitly use the searchable terms "Google Cloud Platform (GCP)", "orchestration", "data ingestion pipelines", "model serving", "monitoring", "data versioning", "LLM", "chat assistant" or "RAG". The missing AI-assistant/RAG and production-operations terms reflect genuine experience gaps and must not be added. The document should, however, make the existing GCP and orchestration experience more explicit without overstating infrastructure ownership.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is partial. The MSc in Statistics is a relevant quantitative degree; Python, feature engineering, cloud-based analytical workflows, batch scoring, Docker, automated testing and scheduled jobs are relevant foundations. The candidate also demonstrates ownership, measurable impact, cross-functional collaboration and internal knowledge sharing, which fit the company’s pragmatic, learning-oriented culture. However, the candidate’s material does not show four years as a Machine Learning Engineer, an AI product such as a chat assistant or RAG system, model serving owned by the candidate, production monitoring, data versioning, or experience with MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool. The current evidence is mainly scheduled notebook forecasting, batch churn scoring and a Streamlit application whose deployment is managed by the platform team. These are genuine role-alignment gaps, not defects that can be solved through wording.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, professional, and unusually careful about distinguishing the candidate's own work from platform-team deployment. It uses quantified outcomes effectively: WAPE improved from 23% to 14%, estimated food waste reduction was 9%, churn was 2.1 percentage points lower in the treated group, and the Streamlit tool was used by approximately 25 people. The progression from Junior Data Analyst to Data Scientist is easy to follow. The main content limitation is not writing quality but role level: the CV presents strong data-science and batch-ML experience, while the target role expects an experienced Machine Learning Engineer operating production AI systems. The document would benefit from more explicit terminology around batch inference, orchestration, automated testing, model evaluation, and data workflows, provided these terms accurately describe the work.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly overall: it uses standard section headings, simple text formatting, conventional date ranges, and searchable technology names such as Python, SQL, GCP, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Docker, pytest, LightGBM, XGBoost, Streamlit, and feature engineering. There are no apparent tables, graphics, columns, headers/footers, or unusual symbols likely to impair parsing. AI screening probability is moderate rather than high for this particular vacancy. Relevant Python, GCP, feature engineering, batch scoring, testing, Docker, and orchestration evidence is present, but the CV has limited or no matching evidence for chat assistants, RAG, language models, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow, or production API deployment. The keyword gap reflects the candidate's documented experience rather than an ATS formatting defect.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the parts of the role involving Python, GCP, feature engineering, model evaluation, experimentation, scheduled workflows, batch scoring, and collaboration with a data platform team. The forecasting workflow and churn model are credible examples of applied ML systems used operationally. The Streamlit application also demonstrates practical software development, Docker usage, testing awareness, and cross-functional adoption. However, the candidate's material shows substantial gaps against the central requirements: the experience is as a Data Scientist rather than four years as an ML Engineer; the documented systems use scheduled notebooks and BigQuery batch scoring rather than API model serving; there is no evidence of chat assistants, RAG, text datasets, language-model fine-tuning, monitoring, or data versioning; and there is no evidence of MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow, or an LLM-observability tool. The MSc in Statistics is a relevant quantitative degree but is not explicitly a degree in machine learning, computer science, or engineering. The profile is therefore a plausible junior or transitional MLE match, but a weak match for the stated seniority and production-AI scope.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the current wording with a version that positions the candidate accurately for this transition and uses supported job terminology: "Data Scientist transitioning toward Machine Learning Engineering, with 4+ years applying Python and statistical modelling to operational forecasting, churn propensity and experimentation. Built scheduled batch-ML workflows on GCP using Vertex AI Workbench and BigQuery, including feature engineering, batch scoring, model evaluation and automated tests. Improved forecast WAPE from 23% to 14% and supported retention targeting that reduced churn by 2.1 percentage points in a holdout evaluation."

2. In the Technical Skills section, reorganise the categories so the strongest job-relevant keywords are easier to parse. Use categories such as: "Programming: Python, SQL, R"; "ML and modelling: LightGBM, XGBoost, scikit-learn, statsmodels, pandas, feature engineering, SHAP"; "Cloud and orchestration: Google Cloud Platform, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt Cloud Scheduler"; and "Software engineering: pytest, Docker, Streamlit, R Markdown, Looker." This makes the existing evidence for Python, GCP, orchestration, feature engineering, and testing more prominent without adding unsupported tools.

3. In the Thistlebox Data Scientist section, change the first two forecasting bullets to make the data workflow and batch-inference terminology explicit while remaining accurate. For example: "Built a weekly batch-forecasting workflow for orders by recipe and region six weeks ahead, using Python, LightGBM and engineered calendar, price and menu-position features." Follow it with: "Orchestrated a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook to generate batch predictions and write forecast outputs to BigQuery for operational reporting in Looker." 

4. In the Thistlebox section, revise the churn bullets to expose the supported pipeline and evaluation keywords: "Built an XGBoost churn-propensity model with engineered customer features and implemented weekly batch scoring in BigQuery; retention offers were targeted to customers in the top decile." Keep the existing 10% holdout bullet immediately after it so the CV clearly shows model evaluation and an outcome.

5. In the Streamlit bullet, preserve the deployment boundary but make the software-engineering contribution more searchable: "Built and containerised a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests; wrote the Python application and Dockerfile, added it to the data platform team's Cloud Run deployment workflow, and supported use by approximately 25 people in product and growth." This wording must not imply that Tobias personally deployed or operated Cloud Run, because the source material says the data platform team handled deployment.

6. In the pytest bullet under Thistlebox, replace "Began writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code in 2025; coverage is approximately 60%" with "Introduced pytest unit tests for forecasting feature-engineering code in 2025; current coverage is approximately 60%." This more directly connects the testing evidence to the job's automated-testing requirement without overstating maturity.

7. In the Selected Project section, retain the label "Personal learning project" in the title or first bullet for the PyTorch work. This is already accurately described, but explicitly labelling it prevents an automated or human reader from interpreting the course project as production AI experience.
